overview: Build a nether portal with crying obsidian and the overworld around it starts to rot: grass to netherrack, water to lava, trees to crimson stems, and mobs into their nether counterparts.
Each crying obsidian block in the frame buys another 64 blocks of radius, so how far it goes is up to you.

1.2.2: A corrupted block keeps the properties it shares with what it becomes.
Water near anything lava could light is left alone. A pond by a house used to take the house.
Lighting a frame with crying obsidian in it earns an advancement.
1.2.1: Crying obsidian frames light again after the game changed the way it checks a portal's shape.
1.2.0: With Village Quests installed, a cleric hands you four stones, one of them crying.
He points you at a half-built doorway a hundred and fifty blocks out.
Far enough that what happens next never reaches the houses. That is the point.
1.0.0: Crying obsidian frames spread corruption outward a block at a time, across two hundred block types.
Mobs on corrupted ground may turn: pig to zombified piglin, villager to zombie villager, slime to magma cube.
